editorial:
Imagine being a teenager who makes a huge mistake just to look cool in front of your friends. That is exactly where you find yourself with Benoît. He loses a silly bet and is forced to ask Aglaée, a girl with a disability, on a date. At first, it feels like a mean prank, but the vibe quickly shifts. You get to see a sweet, awkward friendship grow as Benoît realizes that Aglaée is actually way cooler and more honest than the popular crowd he is trying to impress. It is a lighthearted story about growing up and learning that being kind is more important than being popular.

What really makes this work is the natural acting and the way the pacing keeps you interested without feeling rushed. You will love how the movie handles the humor without being mean-spirited. One downside is that it is a smaller film, so it might feel a bit slow in the middle, but the emotional payoff is totally worth it. If you are looking for a feel-good story, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV or add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you want the best picture quality possible for your home setup.
endingExplained: By the end, Benoît stops caring about his friends' opinions and the bet. He truly falls for Aglaée and realizes his friends are the ones who are actually immature. In the final scenes, he stands up for her and chooses her over the popular group. The movie wraps up with them sharing a genuine connection, showing that a fake start can lead to a real and meaningful relationship. It is a happy, heartwarming finish.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and sweet romances.
